title: Prompt Caching: Stop Paying Full Price for 1 PDF 30x
description:
What is prompt caching? Explained in 60 seconds with one 100-page PDF and 30 questions: the AI saves its work on the PDF, then reuses it while the saved work lasts.
Before, every question re-sent and re-paid the whole PDF at full price (30 questions = 30 PDFs); with prompt caching the PDF part costs about 4 by our math (1.25 for the first question, 0.1 for each later one, the rate on most models; some cost less).

Read the makers' own pages first: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching and https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching

Chapters
0:00 Stop paying full price
0:10 Before: paid thirty times
0:22 Now: the saved work
0:33 How it works, then proof
0:49 The catch: it can fade

The story: one counted example. You load one 100-page PDF and ask your AI 30 questions about it. Without caching, every question sends the whole PDF again and it is read and paid for again at full price, so 30 questions are 30 PDF reads. With prompt caching, the first question pays a quarter more by default (1.25 times the normal input price on Claude, and on OpenAI for GPT-5.6 and later) to save the AI's work on the PDF; questions two to thirty reuse that saved work for about a tenth of the normal price on most models (some models charge less), and usually answer sooner (the makers say caching reduces processing time, but it does not guarantee lower latency).

How it works: the saved work belongs to the unchanged start of the prompt, so the document goes first and stays exactly the same; only the new question at the end is read fresh. The proof is OpenAI's own example: across ten requests, one write and nine reads cost 2.15 times one full read, against 10 times without caching (GPT-5.6 and later, at the 0.1x read rate on most models). The 30-question number is our math, for the PDF part only: 1.25 + 29 x 0.1 = 4.15, so about 4 PDF reads instead of 30, if all 30 questions arrive while the saved work lasts. Your real bill also has the questions and the answers, and some models read for less.

The catch: on Claude, the saved work lasts 5 minutes by default, and unused saved work can fade after a minimum of 5 minutes of inactivity; each use refreshes the clock at no extra cost. OpenAI's default lifetime is 30 minutes for GPT-5.6 and later. Same book: read once, reuse the work, while the saved work lasts.

Sources
Claude docs, Prompt caching: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
OpenAI docs, Prompt caching: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching

The 100-page PDF, the 30 questions, the desk, the student cap and the clock are invented pictures inside the makers' own use case (letting people ask questions about a long document). The robot and the cartoon people are generic drawings, not any maker's artwork or logos.
